discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 121854
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
254 PM EDT Mon Oct 12 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Unseasonably warm conditions continue into Tuesday with record
  or near record high temperatures expected. Tuesday may also 
  approach record warm minimum temperatures for the date.

- Low chances (<20%) for a few showers and storms along and north of 
  US Route 6 tonight.

- Additional periods of greater rain shower chances (40-70%)
  arrive in two waves, one for Tuesday night into early 
  Wednesday afternoon and another wave on Thursday. A few 
  thunderstorms are possible. 

- Turning much cooler for Friday into the weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 245 PM EDT Mon Oct 12 2026

A warm, moist advective regime is underway this afternoon as a 
low level ridge axis continues to shift east of the area. The 
more impressive low level theta-e ridging is expected to develop
this evening from NE KS into SW WI just downstream of a 
progressive weak short wave trough ejecting northeast out of the
northern Rockies. Precip prospects with an initial strong 310K 
isentropic forcing surge early this evening appear to be on the 
low side as better elevated moisture profiles more capable of 
realizing some weak elevated instability will remain displaced 
to the west. By late evening and overnight, isolated showers and
thunderstorms prospects increase as upstream flattening upper 
ridge allows some steeper mid level lapse rates to advect 
eastward to the Mid MS River Valley and southern Great Lakes. 
This later timing will also coincide with the northeast 
progression of the primary low level theta-e ridge and a 
potential of some 500-750 J/kg MUCAPES. Previous forecast 
mention of slight chance PoPs north of US Route 6 still seems 
appropriate as better isentropic forcing and stronger flow on 
310K sfc remain across the north. Cannot completely discount an 
isolated shower south of US Route 6 however, given broad nature 
of advective forcing. 

In terms of temperatures, broad warm advective pattern will allow 
for unseasonably mild min temperatures tonight. Modest low level dew 
points and boundary layer decoupling should allow mins to drop into 
the mid 60s and extent of lows will depend on extent of decoupling 
and the presence of any mid level warm advection-induced 
clouds.

Pre-frontal forcing will begin to shift eastward Tuesday morning 
setting up another warm today for mid-October. The aforementioned 
western Great Lakes short wave will depart to the east, reaching the 
eastern Great Lakes by Tuesday evening. This evolution and southeast 
sinking cut-off upper Low across southwest CONUS will allow 
associated cold frontal boundary to stall across the area Tuesday 
night. Much above normal temperatures will continue Tuesday with 
some uncertainty as to extent of high temperatures. Mixing heights 
may not be particularly deep given very warm low level thermal 
profiles, but even mixing to 900 mb would support high 
temperatures in the low-mid 80s most locations (possibly upper 
80s to around 90 far south). These high temperatures would 
approach or break records for the date of October 13 (84 at FWA 
set in 1975 and 1899 and 86 at SBN set in 1975). Once again, the
extent of lingering mid level cloud will likely play a factor 
in extent of max temps.

By Tuesday night, a plume of higher level theta-e air will advect 
northward into the Mid MS Rvr Valley and eventually the southern 
Great Lakes, while another northern stream trough eventually allows 
for some frontal forcing to interact with this deeper moisture. 
Likely PoPs have been maintained late Tuesday night into early 
Wednesday afternoon with a potential of a few thunderstorms given 
likely presence of elevated instability. Frontal zone once again 
should stall and become less distinct locally later in the day 
Wednesday, setting up a lull in rain chances Wed night into early 
Thu.

Attention will then turn to a stronger short wave amplifying 
across southwest Canada, and potentially phasing with the cut-
off negative upper height anomaly across the Central Plains
towards the end of the work week. GFS deterministic may be a 
bit aggressive in phasing these features when considering bulk 
of GEFS and EC deterministic/ensemble guidance. Nonetheless, 
this northern stream wave will have some good upper level 
dynamics to work with and a stronger eastern Pacific jet to help
induce cyclogenesis across eastern Great Lakes late Thu/Fri. 

Another round of widespread rain is expected Thu/Thu evening as 
another frontal wave develops along the baroclinic zone, 
eventually drying out for Friday outside of some likely lake 
effect rain shower response. Windy conditions are also expected 
Friday, and will depend on extent of low level cyclogenesis and
low level height gradient. However, gusts into the 30 to 40 mph
range look possible during the day Friday given what should be 
fairly deep CAA-induced mixing. Some frost/freeze concerns may 
develop for Friday night/Saturday AM but will depend on 
progression of this pattern and how quickly low level 
anticyclone settles into the area and cloud cover. Greater 
chances of these frost/freeze concerns may hold off until later 
in the weekend. After a transition to below normal temps for the
weekend, temps should moderate back to, or just above normal 
levels early next week with dry weather expected Sat to Mon.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z TAFS THROUGH 18Z TUESDAY/...
Issued at 1208 PM EDT Mon Oct 12 2026

VFR with southwest winds generally hovering around 10 knots
through the period. Low level jet does ramp up a bit tonight as
a frontal wave tracks east through the central Great Lakes. 
This could bring some marginal LLWS to mainly KSBN tonight.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Marsili
AVIATION...Steinwedel

spc.text:
SPC AC 121625

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1125 AM CDT Mon Oct 12 2026

   Valid 121630Z - 131200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Organized severe weather is not forecast across the contiguous
   United States through tonight.

   ...Synopsis...
   Water-vapor imagery late this morning shows a large-scale trough
   over the West.  A lead shortwave disturbance over the Dakotas will
   move east into the Upper Great Lakes by late tonight.  Strengthening
   low-level warm-air advection immediately ahead of a surface low will
   favor scattered thunderstorms developing this evening over parts of
   the Upper Great Lakes and moving into northern MI overnight. 
   Although cloud-bearing shear will be strong, limited elevated
   buoyancy will likely limit updraft strength and a corresponding
   small hail risk with the strongest storms.  

   Moist and moderately strong southwesterly flow aloft will persist
   throughout the eastern periphery of the western CONUS troughing,
   aiding in the development of isolated to scattered thunderstorms. 
   Weak buoyancy should temper overall storm strength, although a
   strong gust or two is possible.

   ..Smith/Guyer.. 10/12/2026

spc.summary: Widely scattered severe storms capable of large hail and damaging winds appear possible over portions of the central and southern Plains into the Lower Missouri Valley Tuesday afternoon into night. More isolated severe weather may occur from southwest Texas into the mid Mississippi Valley, and in parts of New York.
spc.text:
SPC AC 121658

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1158 AM CDT Mon Oct 12 2026

   Valid 131200Z - 141200Z

   ...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PORTIONS OF
   THE SOUTHERN AND CENTRAL PLAINS...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Widely scattered severe storms capable of large hail and damaging
   winds appear possible over portions of the central and southern
   Plains into the Lower Missouri Valley Tuesday afternoon into night.
   More isolated severe weather may occur from southwest Texas into the
   mid Mississippi Valley, and in parts of New York.

   ...Central/Southern Plains to Mid-MS Valley...

   An upper low and attendant trough will migrate east across the
   Southwest on Tuesday, allowing a band of enhanced southwesterly
   mid/upper flow to overspread the region. At the surface, a weak lee
   low and surface trough will develop from western KS through far west
   TX. Meanwhile, a surface cold front will extend from the Upper
   Midwest southwestward through northern KS. This boundary will sag
   south and east through the period. Southerly low-level flow across
   the warm sector between these features will maintain mid 60s to low
   70s F dewpoints across much of the southern Plains into KS and the
   Lower MO Valley. While midlevel lapse rates are expected to remain
   modest across the Plains, heating into the mid 80s to low 90s will
   support moderate destabilization of the very moist airmass, with
   MLCAPE of 1250-2000 J/kg common from parts of northwest TX into the
   Lower MO Valley. 

   Capping is expected to erode by mid to late afternoon, and isolated
   to scattered convection is expected by 00z near the triple point and
   northeast along the cold front into the Lower MO Valley. Additional
   thunderstorms are expected to develop near the surface trough across
   portions of western TX during the evening as a southwesterly
   low-level jet strengthens. Vertically veering wind profiles and 40+
   kt effective shear magnitudes will support initial supercells
   capable of producing large hail and severe wind gusts. Where
   low-level SRH is maximized near the triple point and surface front,
   a tornado or two also could occur. As the low-level jet increases
   and expands northward overnight, additional thunderstorm development
   is expected along and north of the surface front from the Lower MO
   Valley into northern IL. This activity may tend to be elevated on
   the cool side of the surface boundary and pose a risk for marginal
   hail and gusty winds. If convection along the surface can maintain
   near-surface based character, damaging wind potential could be
   greater across parts of MO/IL, but this scenario is uncertain. 

   ...Western NY...

   An upper shortwave trough will shift east from the Upper Great Lakes
   to the Northeast on Tuesday. Deep-layer westerly flow will increase
   across the Lower Great Lakes vicinity as this occurs, and a surface
   low will spread eastward across the region. Ahead of an
   eastward-developing cold front, low to mid 60s F surface dewpoints
   are forecast. While a moist airmass will reside across the region,
   early day clouds and showers/thunderstorms will result in
   questionable destabilization during the afternoon. If sufficient
   destabilization can occur, a few strong thunderstorms could develop
   within the moist and strongly sheared environment, posing a risk of
   locally gusty winds.

   ..Leitman.. 10/12/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 0600Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 121904

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0204 PM CDT Mon Oct 12 2026

   Valid 141200Z - 151200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
   THE SOUTHERN PLAINS AND OZARKS...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Isolated severe thunderstorms are possible across portions of the
   southern Plains into the Ozark Plateau Wednesday afternoon and
   evening.

   ...Southern Plains to the Ozark Plateau...

   Enhanced southwesterly deep-layer flow will persist across the
   region as an upper low develops east/northeast from the Southwest to
   the central High Plains on Wednesday. Surface high pressure is
   forecast to build eastward from the northern Plains to the Great
   Lakes as a surface cold front sags southward from the Ohio Valley
   into the southern Plains. Ahead of this boundary, rich boundary
   layer moisture will be in place, characterized by surface dewpoint
   in the mid 60s to mid 70s F. Showers and thunderstorms will likely
   be ongoing Wednesday morning in the vicinity of the surface front,
   and some downstream cloudiness will likely limit stronger heating
   across portions of the warm sector. Nevertheless, pockets of
   moderate instability are expected to develop from west TX toward the
   Ozark Plateau. As vertical shear and large-scale ascent increase
   during the afternoon, isolated strong to severe storms may develop
   within these pockets of stronger heating and destabilization as the
   surface front sags southward.

   ...Ohio Valley...

   A moist airmass will be in place ahead of a southward-sagging cold
   front. Stronger vertical shear and any appreciable large-scale
   forcing will remain displaced from the warm sector across the Lower
   OH Valley. Modest destabilization will support widely scattered
   thunderstorm develop from the Mid-South into southern OH and parts
   of KY through early evening. However, severe potential is more
   uncertain, compared to portions of the Plains/Ozarks, with northeast
   extent along the surface boundary given poor lapse rates, weaker
   vertical shear and nebulous large-scale ascent.

   ..Leitman.. 10/12/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
